messages:
alex: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing an SLO-backed changefeed strategy for the metering/billing pipeline. High level: produce an enriched changefeed (billing-events) from ingest, maintain per-tenant checkpoints, and rely on per-partition monotonic sequences + idempotency keys for credits. Thoughts?

mira: Sounds promising. main worry is out-of-order arrivals from cross-region mirrors and how that affects attribution/dedupe.

dan: We can attach a monotonic usage_seq at ingest time per token/tenant. Changefeed only needs to guarantee per-partition order. seq + event_id covers idempotency.

jamie: Auditability question — auditors may want raw-event replay with original attribution pointers. Will checkpoints and enrichment lose fidelity?

alex: No — raw events preserved in cold storage (JSONL) for 90 days. Changefeed emits references: {raw_id, fingerprint, enriched_payload_ref}. That keeps a canonical replay path.

rika: Cross-region lag edge-case: late arrivals could re-order seqs. Suggest per-tenant watermark + configurable lag tolerance window (e.g., 2m default). If event arrives beyond watermark, emit a "late-arrival" tag for downstream reconcile.

mira: Also propose integrating with the existing handshake: emit explicit commit markers when tenant checkpoint advances so consumers can compact state safely.

dan: Implementation sketch: 1) PoC service reads ingest log (append-only), applies enrichment rules, publishes to Kafka topic billing-events-v2. 2) Router consumers do attribution/crediting using idempotent upserts. 3) Checkpointer writes per-tenant offset to Dynamo (lease-protected).

jamie: Operational SLOs? For hosted customers we want 99.9% on-time delivery. What metrics + alerts do we need?

alex: Minimal metric set: lag_ms per-tenant (p50/p95/p99), percent of events exceeding SLA, replays/sec, late-arrival ratio. Alert on p95 lag > 5s or sustained increase x2 baseline for 10m.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary started for billing-events-v2 PoC -> namespace: staging -> id: canary-21

jamie: Good — rollback criteria: lag spike > 2x baseline or dedupe failure > 0.05% in 5m window.

mira: Dedupe window: heavy token churn in some tenants. Default 3m seems reasonable but should be tenant-configurable.

dan: Agreed. Use fingerprint + seq + tenant_id for dedupe keys. Make window configurable by tenant profile.

alex: Audit trail plan: provenance envelope appended to changefeed messages: {raw_id, ingest_ts, enriched_ts, fingerprint, enrichment_version}. We'll persist full envelopes in S3 (JSONL) and index minimal metadata (raw_id -> s3_path) in ES for quick lookups.

rika: Backfill story: when enrichment rules change we can re-run raw events through enrichment and emit a special "reconcile" event that downstreams use to re-evaluate credits/quality. Keep reconcile events idempotent and mark them as replays.

jamie: Cost note: PoC will double-write to cold storage for a short time; estimate +8% storage. But helps forensic queries and audits.

mira: Failover/double-charge prevention: checkpoint writer must hold a lease; consumers must apply credits idempotently using event_id as upsert key. Also have a fast repair job that compares credits vs expected for a sample.

dan: Crediting design: consumer writes an idempotency record (event_id -> applied_at, version) then conditional upsert to credits ledger. If consumer retries, conditional upsert prevents double-charge.

alex: Next steps: I'll open an RFC PR with sequence diagrams, metric list, rollout plan (staging canary -> limited-prod -> global), and a short PoC task list. Assign reviewers: @mira @dan @jamie.

rika: :thumbsup:

jamie: Spike assignment: dan + rika to prototype read->enrich->kafka path next week. Keep it minimal: enrichment rules, fingerprinting, emit commit markers.

alex: Great — please drop small PR with PoC notes and onboarding steps. We'll reconvene mid-week after spike.
